status.en: 120 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 29% fewer than the week before, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Kaduna.
status.nb: 120 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 29 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Gunmen continue to target civilians in Plateau State, killing three miners at an illegal mining site, injuring others, and raiding a community where they abducted five people and shot two. Fulani herders expressed anger over a crackdown in Plateau, while a priest was left unconscious after an attack in Benue State and a Nigerian immigrant severed a Malaysian police officer's wrist before being shot dead. Tensions flared in Kaduna as residents reported an attack on Muslims during a burial, which police dispute as a religious clash. The conflict recorded 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpenmenn fortsetter å angripe sivile i Plateau State, dreper tre gruvearbeidere på en ulovlig gruvested, skader andre, og ransaker et samfunn hvor de bortførte fem personer og skjøt to. Fulani-gjetere uttrykte sinne over en nedslag i Plateau, mens en prest ble liggende bevisstløs etter et angrep i Benue State og en nigeriansk innvandrer kappet en malaysisk politimann i håndleddet før han ble skutt og drept. Spenningene blusset opp i Kaduna da innbyggere rapporterte et angrep på muslimer under en begravelse, noe politiet bestrider som en religiøs konflikt. Konflikten registrerte 1 486 dødsfall knyttet til kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
